## Abiotic Variables {.topic-abiotic .topic-icon}

The [abiotic data]{.abiotic} in the [VegVault]{.vegvault} database provide essential information on [environmental factors]{.abiotic} affecting vegetation distribution and [traits]{.traits}.
Currently, [VegVault]{.vegvault} includes [abiotic data]{.abiotic} from [CHELSA](https://chelsa-climate.org/), [CHELSA-TRACE21](https://doi.org/10.16904/envidat.211), and the [Harmonized World Soil Database (HWSD) v2.2](https://data.apps.fao.org/catalog/iso/ff5c613c-75bb-46a9-a162-bc728059b465).
[CHELSA]{.abiotic} and [CHELSA-TRACE21]{.abiotic} provide high-resolution [climate data]{.abiotic}, while [HWSD]{.abiotic} offers detailed [soil information]{.abiotic}.
VegVault 1.0.0 named the soil source WoSIS; it was HWSD v2.0 or v2.01 (the exact version was not recorded).

### Abiotic variables (`AbioticVariable`) {.topic-abiotic}

As [VegVault]{.vegvault} contains [abiotic variables]{.abiotic} from several [primary sources]{.database}, the `AbioticVariable` table contains descriptions of [abiotic variables]{.abiotic} (`abiotic_variable_name`), their units (`abiotic_variable_unit`), and measurement details (`measure_details`). These data include variables such as [climate]{.abiotic} and [soil conditions]{.abiotic}, which are crucial for understanding the ecological contexts of vegetation dynamics. 

```{r}
#| label: AbioticVariable variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `AbioticVariable`."
data_comments_abiotic_variable <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "abiotic_variable_id", "ID of a Abiotic Variable",
    "abiotic_variable_name", "Name of a Abiotic Variable from primary source",
    "abiotic_variable_unit", "Unit of a Abiotic Variable",
    "measure_details", "Additional details about Abiotic Variable"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "AbioticVariable"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_abiotic_variable,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: AbioticVariable scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/AbioticVariable.svg"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: show abiotic variables
#| tbl-cap: "Table showing abiotic variables."
dplyr::tbl(con, "AbioticVariable") %>%
  dplyr::select(abiotic_variable_name, abiotic_variable_unit, measure_details) %>%
  dplyr::collect() %>%
  rlang::set_names(
    nm = c(
      "Variable name",
      "Variable unit",
      "Source of data"
    )
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

Some properties of the values need attention:

- `bio4` (temperature seasonality) is in hundredths of a degree Celsius, as its unit says; in VegVault 1.0.0, the present-day `bio4` was 0 south of about 65.7° N because of a truncated download.
- A present-day `bio12` (annual precipitation) of 6553.5 kg m^-2^ is the storage limit of CHELSA V2.1, so it is a lower bound.
- CHELSA-TRACE21 stores precipitation in whole kg m^-2^, so a dry quarter with less than 0.5 kg m^-2^ is 0 in the past (`bio18`, `bio19`), while the present-day values come in steps of 0.1.
- In the Sahel and the Sudanian belt, the coldest quarter of `bio19` can be the dry winter in one product and the rainy season in the other, so `bio19` can change between 0 and several hundred kg m^-2^ between the present day and the past.

### Abiotic Data (`AbioticData`) {.topic-abiotic}

The `AbioticData` table holds the actual values of abiotic variables (the units are the same for each `AbioticVariable`).

```{r}
#| label:  AbioticData variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `AbioticData`."
data_comments_abiotic_data <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "sample_id", "ID of a Sample",
    "abiotic_variable_id", "ID of an Abiotic Variable",
    "abiotic_value", "Value of an Abiotic Variable"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "AbioticData"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_abiotic_data,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(

  )
)
```


### Gridpoints (`AbioticDataReference`) {.topic-abiotic}

```{r}
#| label: link-limits
#| include: false

link_distance_km <-
  load_config_value(value = c("link", "distance_km"))

link_distance_years <-
  load_config_value(value = c("link", "distance_years"))
```

Gridpoints are stored in artificially created [Datasets]{.database} and [Samples]{.database}, with one [Dataset]{.database} holding more [Samples]{.database} only if they differ in age.
We have estimated the spatial and temporal distance between each [gridpoint]{.abiotic} and other non-[gridpoint]{.abiotic} [Samples]{.database} (`vegetation_plot`, `fossil_pollen_archive`, and `traits`).
We store the link between [gridpoint]{.abiotic} and non-[gridpoint]{.abiotic} [Samples]{.database} as well as the spatial and temporal distance.
A link is kept when the two are at most `r link_distance_km` km and at most `r scales::label_comma()(link_distance_years)` years apart, and any [gridpoint]{.abiotic} [Sample]{.database} without a link is discarded as not relevant for the vegetation dynamics.

Since VegVault 2.0.0, the links are stored once per position, a distinct combination of longitude, latitude and age, because many [Samples]{.database} share a position.
`AbioticDataReference` is a view, a stored query: it combines the tables `SamplePosition` (the position of each non-[gridpoint]{.abiotic} [Sample]{.database}) and `PositionLink` (the [gridpoints]{.abiotic} linked to each position) and returns one row per [Sample]{.database} and linked [gridpoint]{.abiotic}, with the same columns as the table `AbioticDataReference` of VegVault 1.0.0.
The positions themselves are in the table `Positions`.

```{r}
#| label: AbioticDataReference variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for view `AbioticDataReference`."
data_comments_abiotic_data_reference <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "sample_id", "ID of non-gridpoint Sample",
    "sample_ref_id", "ID of gridpoint Sample",
    "distance_in_km", "Distance among samples expressed in kilometres",
    "distance_in_years", "Distance among samples expressed in years"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "AbioticDataReference"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_abiotic_data_reference,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```


Such data structure allows that environmental context is readily available for each vegetation and trait [Sample]{.database}. For each non-[gridpoint]{.abiotic} [Sample]{.database}, users can select the closest spatio-temporally abiotic data or get average from all surrounding [gridpoints]{.abiotic}.

```{r}
#| label: distribution of gridpoints
x_lim <- c(12, 18.9)
y_lim <- c(48.5, 51.1)

x_lim_min <- min(x_lim)
x_lim_max <- max(x_lim)
y_lim_min <- min(y_lim)
y_lim_max <- max(y_lim)

data_grid_coord <-
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "Datasets"),
    dplyr::tbl(con, "DatasetTypeID"),
    by = "dataset_type_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "gridpoints") %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    coord_long >= !!rlang::enquo(x_lim_min) &
      coord_long <= !!rlang::enquo(x_lim_max)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    coord_lat >= !!rlang::enquo(y_lim_min) &
      coord_lat <= !!rlang::enquo(y_lim_max)
  )

data_grid_coord_local <-
  dplyr::collect(data_grid_coord)

# The spacing of the grid, from the distinct longitudes of the gridpoints
value_grid_step <-
  data_grid_coord_local %>%
  dplyr::distinct(coord_long) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(coord_long) %>%
  dplyr::pull(coord_long) %>%
  base::diff() %>%
  stats::median()

fig_data_grid_coord <-
  data_grid_coord_local %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long,
      y = coord_lat
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(
    xlim = x_lim,
    ylim = y_lim
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Gridpoints in Czechia",
    subtitle = stringr::str_c(
      "One gridpoint about every ",
      base::round(value_grid_step, 2),
      " degrees"
    ),
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = NA,
    col_line = col_blue_light, # [config]
    linewidth = line_size * 10 # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    shape = 22,
    size = point_size / 2,
    stroke = 0.3,
    fill = col_green_dark,
    colour = col_white
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_data_grid_coord)
```

```{r}
#| label: exampe of abitic data - bio1

# Acess the VegVault file
plan_example_all <-
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(
    path = path_to_vegvault # [config]
  ) %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "gridpoints"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to Czech Republic
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = c(48.5, 51.1),
    long_lim = c(12, 18.9)
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # select only modern data
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(0, 0)
  ) %>%
  # Add abiotic data
  vaultkeepr::get_abiotic_data() %>%
  # Select only Mean Anual Temperature (bio1)
  vaultkeepr::select_abiotic_var_by_name(sel_var_name = "bio1")

data_example_all <-
  vaultkeepr::extract_data(
    con = plan_example_all,
    return_raw_data = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  )

# The extraction leaves the connection of the plan open
DBI::dbDisconnect(purrr::chuck(plan_example_all, "db_con"))

data_gridpoints_abiotic <-
  data_example_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "gridpoints") %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat, sample_id_link) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .fn = ~ paste0(.x, "_grid")
  )

data_vegetation <-
  data_example_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "vegetation_plot") %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .fn = ~ paste0(.x, "_veg")
  )

data_links <-
  data_gridpoints_abiotic %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    data_vegetation,
    by = c("sample_id_link_grid" = "sample_id_veg")
  )

# A band of the area, so that the single links can be seen; at 50 degrees
#   N, 4 degrees of longitude by 1 of latitude fill the width of the figure
x_lim_links <- c(13, 17)
y_lim_links <- c(49.5, 50.5)

fig_gridpoint_links_example <-
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(
    xlim = x_lim_links,
    ylim = y_lim_links
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Links between vegetation plots and gridpoints",
    subtitle = stringr::str_c(
      "Part of Czechia, ", x_lim_links[1], " to ", x_lim_links[2],
      " degrees E and ", y_lim_links[1], " to ", y_lim_links[2],
      " degrees N"
    ),
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    caption = "Squares: gridpoints. Dots: vegetation plots. Lines: links."
  ) +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = NA,
    col_line = col_blue_light, # [config]
    linewidth = line_size * 10 # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = data_links,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long_grid,
      y = coord_lat_grid,
      xend = coord_long_veg,
      yend = coord_lat_veg
    ),
    col = col_white,
    linewidth = line_size * 4
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = data_gridpoints_abiotic,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long_grid,
      y = coord_lat_grid
    ),
    shape = 22,
    size = point_size,
    stroke = 0.3,
    fill = col_green_dark,
    colour = col_white
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = data_vegetation,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long_veg,
      y = coord_lat_veg
    ),
    shape = 20,
    alpha = 0.75,
    size = point_size * 0.75,
    col = col_green_light
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_gridpoint_links_example)

```

### Abiotic Variable Reference (`AbioticVariableReference`) {.topic-abiotic}

Each [Abiotic Variable]{.abiotic} can have a separate [Reference]{.database}, in addition to a [Dataset]{.database} and [Sample]{.database}. 

```{r}
#| label: AbioticVariableReference variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `AbioticVariableReference`."
data_comments_abiotic_variable_reference <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "abiotic_variable_id", "ID of an Abiotic Variable",
    "reference_id", "ID of a Reference"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  table_name = "AbioticVariableReference"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_abiotic_variable_reference,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```
